candidates.title: Meet the Trains.com team at Trainfest 2026
candidates.excerpt: Trainfest, America’s largest operating model railroad show, returns to Milwaukee again this November 7th and 8th. This year’s show promises to be bigger than ever, with over 250 vendor booths, 500 tables, and more than 50 operating train layouts and displays. Trainfest will be held in downtown Milwaukee’s Baird Center, and will be hosted by the National Model Railroad Association (NMRA), which became the show’s producer last year to celebrate its 90 th anniversary. You can buy tickets now by visiting trainfest.com, where you can also view the “how-to” clinic schedule, nearby hotels and event parking. The staff of both Model Railroader and Trains magazines will be there in a special Firecrown Media booth to meet visitors and answer questions. We’ll also be doing live manufacturer and layout interviews, which we’ll livestream to both Facebook and Trains.com. If you can’t watch live, the videos will be available on Trains.com. candidates.title: NTSB releases final report on fatal accident involving BNSF conductor in Montana
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — A lack of a requirement to establish on-track safety while releasing brakes on a parked train, coupled with an inadequate safety briefing about the hazards of the work location, played a part in the October 2025 death of a BNSF conductor, the National Transportation Safety Board said in its final investigation report. The conductor was struck by a passing train on Oct. 19, 2025, at a location in Columbus, Mont., where the NTSB said “it would be difficult to work without accidentally fouling the main track.” The conductor and an engineer had been assigned to operate a westbound manifest freight parked in the siding at Columbus. At about 9:32 a.m., while the conductor was in the process of releasing hand brakes, he stepped into the adjacent main track and was struck by an eastbound empty grain train. Shipbuilding sources place the latest vessels at the group’s Yantai Raffles facility for delivery in 2030, extending a relationship that has already produced four LNG dual-fuel car carriers for the Oslo-based tonnage provider. candidates.excerpt: IMEC and The Hood launch Sisterhood Box to support the next generation of female seafarers The International Maritime Employers’ Council (IMEC) and The Hood Platform have joined forces to launch the Sisterhood Box, a new initiative providing female cadets with practical support as they take their first steps into life at sea. The first 47 Sisterhood Boxes were presented to female cadets at the Maritime Academy of Asia and the Pacific (MAAP) in the Philippines, bringing together two complementary initiatives: IMEC’s focus on period dignity and welfare for cadets, and The Hood’s Sisterhood initiative to create a stronger support network for female seafarers. The project hopes to spark a movement in the industry through challenging leaders to look more closely at whether women are being given the support they need not only to enter the profession, but to remain and build lasting careers within it. candidates.title: Hapag-Lloyd’s dual-fuel vessel bunkered with bio-methanol in Busan
candidates.excerpt: Hapag-Lloyd’s dual-fuel vessel bunkered with bio-methanol in Busan German shipping firm Hapag-Lloyd has bunkered one of its dual-fuel vessels with an unspecified quantity of bio-methanol at the Port of Busan in South Korea. The methanol-capable container ship Seaspan Amazon received the stem while simultaneously unloading cargo at the port. The bio-methanol was produced at Chinese renewable energy firm Goldwind’s facility in Hinggan League, Inner Mongolia. Hapag-Lloyd did not disclose the physical supplier that delivered the fuel in Busan. The bunkering operation forms part of a long-term supply agreement Hapag-Lloyd signed with Goldwind in 2024. Under the deal, Goldwind is expected to supply 250,000 mt/year of a blend of bio- and e-methanol from the end of 2027. By securing an early delivery under the agreement, the companies have gained operational experience with fuel handling. candidates.excerpt: Invesco taps Finnish wealth manager for Nordic capital Invesco has partnered with Finnish wealth manager Index Varainhoito to open its European Upper Middle Market Income Fund (EUMMI) to Nordic investors. The global asset manager said the deal extends the strategy’s reach across Europe’s wealth market and marks the fund’s first distribution agreement with a Nordic wealth management platform. Launched in December 2025, EUMMI is an evergreen fund structured under the ELTIF 2.0 framework. candidates.title: CSX Santa Train sets annual trip for Nov. 21
candidates.excerpt: KINGSPORT, Tenn. — The CSX Santa Train is set to make its 84th trip through Appalachia on Nov. 21, CSX and the North Pole Transportation Authority have announced. The train will follow the 110-mile route through Kentucky, Virginia, and Tennessee that has been a tradition since 1943, delivering toys, gifts, and winter clothing items at stops between Shelbiana, Ky., and Kingsport. “As we look ahead to a new year, we’re reminded that the CSX Santa Train is about so much more than a journey along the tracks,” said Tom Livingston, CSX vice president of government and community affairs. “It’s about bringing people together, creating moments of joy and carrying traditions forward from one generation to the next. The warmth of the communities that welcome the CSX Santa Train and the support from people across the country remind us why this tradition has endured for generations.” Scheduled stops for the Nov. 21 trip include: Kentucky - Shelby, 6 a.m. - Marrowbone, 6:20 a.m. - Elkhorn City, 7:05

candidates.excerpt: Tikehau opens credit fund to wealth managers via iCapital Tikehau Capital has made its European private credit strategy available on iCapital Marketplace as the French alternative asset manager looks to attract more capital from wealthy investors.
